text: Today’s students grow up in the age where their surroundings are determined primarily by technological connectivity. With the introduction of technology into life, people have gained the chance to get information promptly. The fact that every student and teacher live in the world of screens makes the communication style between them change drastically. Nevertheless, this transition to digital communication has also caused various issues, like cyberbullying, harassment, and even concealed emotional problems.

text: To handle these modern issues, modern means should be used. Given that most of the student interaction is conducted via electronic devices, technologies should be used actively to prevent any harmful actions. Using technologies will make it possible to trace bullying or other risky behavior of students with the help of software applications rather than only relying on traditional control measures. In case when the administration uses sophisticated monitoring methods, it will be able to track all digital communications and get immediate alerts regarding any critical behavior of the student.

text: In an effort to enable schools such as St. Vincent Blessed School of Manila (SVBSM) to effectively identify and mitigate risks in students, the developers came up with StudentShield, which is a complete solution that helps mitigate the effects of peer victimization both socially and psychologically. Unlike the conventional way of dealing with student risks where the user is always expected to constantly keep on checking the dashboard, StudentShield incorporates a module for sending emails automatically whenever there is a risk through the use of the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP).

text: In this model, the analysis of the texts with natural language processing allows us to classify the emotion level into four different risk categories: low, medium, high, and critical. Such an analysis can generate instant alerts to the concerned people, especially to the guidance counselor when there is a critical behavioural risk identified. Hence, this will allow the StudentShield to provide real-time notifications to the concerned party regarding the threat to students' safety. Data privacy and security was a major concern in the design of the machine learning model because the data involved are private information about students.

text: The proposed study would provide a tremendous enhancement to the way the student wellbeing at Saint Vincent Blessed School of Manila is maintained. The traditional environment would focus on solving disciplinary and wellness problems reactively after they have become publicly known. text: StudentShield offers students a safe space to share their thoughts without feeling immediately judged by all but assured there is help available should anything happen. Students can express themselves in a conditional anonymous manner and vent what they want without fear since the system knows their identity. It acts like an automated assistance counselor for the guidance counselors in filtering through several vents and focusing on High and Critical cases thereby minimizing the daily work of counselors.

text: Parents are also the weakest link in the security of schools due to the fact that they are also the last to know about any issues that may arise involving their children. The solution to that is to give the students an instant response system. If the issue is life-threatening or aggressively violent in nature, then the NLP engine automatically sends an alert to the parent. Thus, the parent would be notified instantly about the situation which needs immediate intervention both at home and at school. Parents can receive automated emails and get a real-time notification regarding the psychological state of the child and cyber-bullying.

text: As reported by Zhang, T., Schoene, A.M., Ji, S. et al. (2022), natural language processing algorithms have the capacity to identify signs of depression, anxiety, and suicide risk using non-clinical text such as tweets and postings on forums. According to the authors' findings, pre-trained models pick up on emotional cues that cannot be easily detected using traditional questionnaires and that are frequently ignored by younger individuals in favor of expressing them through digital platforms. In addition to this, it was highlighted that pre-trained models lack accuracy when dealing with language patterns not commonly included in the training set.

text: This book explores bullying and Cyberbullying from diverse perspectives, including its frequency, context, and repercussions. According to Fermani et al. (2023), here are some of the issues that do not arise with traditional bullying but come up in cyberbullying: once a message has been put up, it will remain visible for an indefinite amount of time, thus creating a vast audience base, and perpetrators can quickly assume anonymity. The studies conducted by Stuart have shown that the repercussions faced by students who encounter both types of bullying were much worse than those suffered by victims of either form of harassment alone.

text: Mnassri et al. (2022) point out that stacking multiple BERT-based models and then voting on the results decreases false positives in hate speech detection. According to their research conducted at the IEEE Global Communications Conference, there is no BERT configuration that prevails in all cases of hate speech. Therefore, multiple configurations can ensure safer prediction.

text: According to Malam et al. (2020), traditional binary classification models that merely label text as "bullying" or "non-bullying" fail to provide actionable context for institutional intervention. In their study, machine learning classifiers were trained to categorize text into four distinct severity levels (None, Low, Medium, and High), demonstrating that multi-level severity scoring allows responders to differentiate routine insults from high-harm threats. Complementing this, EMNLP Findings (2022) and Fodeh et al. (2022) applied natural language processing to stratify text-based psychological distress into four risk tiers (Low, Moderate/Medium, High, and Critical/Severe). Their research highlighted that isolating a dedicated Critical tier is essential for identifying emergency scenarios such as explicit self-harm or severe harassment that necessitate immediate escalation and intervention.

text: StudentShield adopts this exact multi-level risk architecture by mapping analyzed student entries into four structured risk bands: Low (1%–30%), Medium (31%–60%), High (61%–85%), and Critical (86%–100%). text: The proponents relate it to the present study because StudentShield should be preventative rather than reactionary. Therefore, the technology should detect the signs of deteriorating mental state prior to a crisis taking place, not just react after something went wrong. text: Based on the results of Asghar et al. (2022), there are NLP screening tools that may be able to spot high-school students suffering from emotional distress, based on their writing assignments. In their study, they found out that the screening tool was equally effective compared to clinical screening methods used by medical professionals. They advised that the tools should be used as a "first-pass" filter for schools.

text: The proponents have connected this to the current study since their product, the StudentShield, is precisely designed according to this concept. This is done in such a way that the AI engine serves only as a digital "first-responder," but not as a substitute for a counselor. It works by screening vents for any potential problem cases that are referred to the human counselor for a final decision. This is why the proponents decided to use this approach after learning about it through the research of Asghar et al. (2022)

text: Roy and Kumar (2025) findings reveal that hate speech models perform poorly when used for classification of code-switched text messages in which users use two or more languages to form a single sentence. The models classified many toxic tweets as neutral tweets due to code-switching. Multilingual Transformers performed better, although they had to be fine-tuned on the code-switched examples in the target language pair.

text: As stated in Santiago et al. (2023), their online sentiment analysis system utilized to guide the counseling offices in Cavite province involved capturing short messages from the students through simple NLP and classifying these messages based on the prevailing mood conveyed. The transition from traditional pen-and-paper process saved the counselors more time while making it easy to detect if there is a downward trend in the students' mood during a certain period of weeks.

text: Based on the findings of Shannen et al. (2021), more than half of the students surveyed in the population of Metro Manila were victims of cyberbullying in the previous semester and had experienced high levels of anxiety during the tests as opposed to the normal population. Moreover, Shannen et al. (2021) have shown that more than half of the victims failed to report their situation to school officials.

text: According to Soylemez (2023), most Filipino parents lack adequate technological knowledge and resources to prevent their kids from potential dangers in the cyber world. Parents relied heavily on non-technical measures to find solutions to the problem and preferred imposing time restrictions over monitoring software. The current study sheds light on the importance of the technology in schools for cooperation between schools and parents.

They recommended automating the documentation process whenever possible.

The key point was not convenience, but the degree of privacy of information revealed during consultations.

text: As Cruz and Cheng (2022) note, transfer learning that uses fine-tuning of pre-trained models on the basis of a language with many available resources (English) and adapts them to the use of the Filipino language, which is resource-poor, is highly useful. According to the results obtained by Cruz and Cheng, multilingual BERT models, which were fine-tuned for the Filipino language, considerably outperformed those trained on a small data set from scratch.

text: The StudentShield project follows the concept of decoupling, where the application is made up of two different parts, namely, a web application and machine learning analysis. The separation was aimed at ensuring that there would be no crashes in the submission process for the students. Decoupling was implemented to ensure that the machine learning algorithm had sufficient computing power to analyze multiple texts simultaneously. This is particularly relevant during busy periods such as exams when the number of students increases drastically.

text: Advanced Language Models: Distress detection and emotional classification in this paper employs the use of mDeBERTa-v3 together with the 28-class GoEmotions multilabel classifier. The transformers were chosen due to their proven strength in processing the kind of multilingual, Taglish, and gen Z type of informal language commonly spoken by junior high school students. Using mDeBERTa’s understanding of the Taglish language and GoEmotions’ advanced multilabel classifier, it will be possible to detect the psychological states contained in informal student responses. For the fine-tuning process, a dataset that is built on text submission of the students from SVBSM Junior High School will be used to analyze the linguistic structure and emotional tone in all of the 28 emotions. At least 300 labeled text data sets will be gathered based on validation done by the guidance counselors in the school, with data augmentation applied to ensure at least 1,000 samples for the training process.

text: Vectorized Trajectory Tracking: The system uses FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) to vectorize the submissions for trajectory analysis. With this ability, StudentShield compares the student’s last submission against the last two weeks of submissions to detect emotional changes in the state.

text: Development Software: The entire technology stack comprises the use of PHP 8 and CodeIgniter 4 as backend technologies; Python and FastAPI to build the predictive microservice, HuggingFace transformers such as mDeBERTa-v3 model for prediction of threat levels and GoEmotions model for predicting multi-label emotions; and FAISS-Powered Predictive Recurrence Memory. The rest include MySQL for AES-256 Encryption of Data Storage; Local SMS Gateway for Emergency Routing and InfinityFree/Microsoft Azure Cloud Hosting Platform.

text: Output represents the final phase in the process of finalizing the deliverables of the project. Deliverables include the fully-fledged StudentShield system that consists of an encrypted Safe Space Website, predictive emotion analysis tools for detecting bullying and depression, In-app Online Video Conferencing Integration, and Confidentiality Shielding, among others. Additionally, the system generates Predictive Risk and Recurrence Assessment Scores, automatic SMS and email alerts sent to parents in case of emergencies, and campus-wide trends based on the Counselor Dashboard analysis.

text: Machine Learning - Subfield of artificial intelligence that enables computers to learn from experience and adapt without being explicitly programmed (Mitchell, 1997). Machine learning is the main element in the development of a system to recognize patterns of bullying and emotional distress in Taglish text submissions. Microservice - An architectural method for developing a single application as a suite of small running services (Fowler, 2014). A way of building software where different parts run independently. In the StudentShield system, the AI engine works independently from the primary website to maintain the overall system efficiency during text analysis.

text: tem that monitors and scores student distress text into four severity bands (Low, Medium, High, or Critical). It begins by calculating a Base Score using a weighted mix of machine learning models that detect toxic or distressed text, negative emotions, and semantic similarity to crisis phrases. Next, it applies Heuristics boosts including an exponential compound multiplier if it flags specific indicators like hopelessness, masked depression, or isolation. For immediate safety, Hard Overrides can instantly bypass the scoring to force a High or Critical rating for explicit self-harm, violence, or final planning, while safely downgrading genuine sarcasm. Finally, it uses Historical Tracking (FAISS) over a 14-day window to escalate a student's risk level if it detects a worsening emotional trajectory or chronic, repeating distress incidents.

text: The main goal of StudentShield's design was to maintain that the system is always fast and responsive even when students submit long messages. To do this, we decided to split the system between a machine learning engine and a web interface. Because of its unique design, the website for students or counselors won't be slowed down by the challenging process of text analysis. Each feature of the system was chosen to support a secure and stable environment for the benefit of students.

text: The diagram highlights a student safety system that calls for three primary user roles: students, administrators (or school counselors), and parents. Besides administrators or counselors having access to a dashboard where they can review complaints, analyze behavior, and settle the problem, students can also make an conditional anonymous complaint through the website or app. Data is kept in a MySQL database, and the back-end handles roles, user authentication, and simple service calls. In addition, it uses NLP/machine learning capabilities for risk assessment purposes and integration with third-party applications like email and SMS notifications. The FastAPI ML Engine, along with its FAISS vector memory, is packaged as a Docker container and deployed directly to Hugging Face Spaces, functioning as an isolated microservice.

text: Based on the Level 0 Data Flow Diagram, StudentShield is seen as the key system that serves as the communication channel between the student, counselor, or super admin, parent, or guardian, and the HuggingFace ML microservice. The students are able to enter their login credentials to log in and submit their venting logs and reports of any bullying they encounter. As input to the system, the output from the system is the session token and confirmation of status as a way of letting the student know that the action was processed. The FastAPI ML Engine, along with its FAISS vector memory, is packaged as a Docker container and deployed directly to Hugging Face Spaces, functioning as an isolated microservice.

text: The system passes on the vent text to the HuggingFace ML microservice, which outputs the risk score and emotion class, helping the system to detect cases that might need attention. The system generates notifications and dashboard information to be sent to the counselors or super admins while at the same time the counselors and super admins provide case verification and system configurations to the system. Where there are cases of potential danger, the parent or guardian receives SMS and email notifications.

text: While the Context Diagram presents StudentShield as one system, DFD Level 1 reveals what happens inside the system. The process consists of the following: Manage User Accounts, Analyze Vent Submissions, Process Bullying Reports, Monitor Cases & Analytics, and Dispatch Notifications. Manage User Accounts verifies the user's credentials in the User/Profile Records repository, containing users, students, counselors, and admins. All the significant events related to the management process are recorded in Audit Logs.

text: If a student sends their vent, the system sends it to the HuggingFace ML Service, which generates a classification based on risks associated with the event. Afterward, the event is stored in vent_logs, and a confirmed alert is generated if necessary. Bullying reports are processed in the Process Bullying Reports process and stored in bully_reports. The Monitor Cases and Analytics process permits the counselor and the super admin to view user records, vent records, and reports. All their actions are saved. In the end, notifications are dispatched via the Local SMS Gateway and Gmail SMTP Server. All the messages are stored in sms_logs and email_logs. The FastAPI ML Engine, along with its FAISS vector memory, is packaged as a Docker container and deployed directly to Hugging Face Spaces, functioning as an isolated microservice.

Afterward, the event is stored in vent_logs, and a confirmed alert is generated if necessary. Bullying reports are processed in the Process Bullying Reports process and stored in bully_reports. The Monitor Cases and Analytics process permits the counselor and the super admin to view user records, vent records, and reports. All their actions are saved. In the end, notifications are dispatched via the Local SMS Gateway and Gmail SMTP Server. All the messages are stored in sms_logs and email_logs. The FastAPI ML Engine, along with its FAISS vector memory, is packaged as a Docker container and deployed directly to Hugging Face Spaces, functioning as an isolated microservice.</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr></w:r></w:p>

text: Firstly, the researchers establish what problem this study is intended to solve when developing the research plan. In the school setting, there was no established procedure for identifying cases of bullying, problems of students, and any other issues that would need assistance. This provides a basis for the purpose of StudentShield. The system was developed to assist the parents and counselors in getting real-time information, identifying the issues from the text, and creating a safe platform where the students can vent their feelings. This is the stage at which the system components were introduced.

text: The researchers analyzed the needs of the system based on the needs of the users during the process of system analysis. It was necessary to establish the way in which the system would analyze the texts in order to establish possible levels of threats, the way in which counselors will view the reports and the way in which the students will report bullying and venting messages. Database architecture, user privileges, encryption of sensitive information, implementation of machine learning and warning systems were some of the technical needs that were analyzed.

text: During the system design phase, the StudentShield structure was carefully designed. The researchers developed the database structure, arranged the fundamental components of the system, and determined the relationships between the most essential parts. Also, counselors' and students' user interfaces were created with ease of use and procedure simplicity in mind. As well, the interface between the web application and machine learning service was highlighted, especially with the topic of notification management, risk assessment, and text classification. Process flowcharts, architecture diagrams, and entity-relationship diagrams were one of the design outputs used as deployment tools.

text: The super admin workflow is the process of managing the system using the verification and administration process. The process involves the need to provide a password and an email for one to log into the system. Once the submission is made successfully, the system initiates the two factor authentication process in order to verify the identity of the administrator. The system offers the real time monitoring of intelligence flows, incident reports, and delivery status of alerts. The user administration features include viewing system databases, creating user account, editing and deleting users' profile among others.

text: Methodology used by the counselor is intended for observation as well as response. Entry into the system is done through secure log-in and use of two-factor authentication. The main work area will be dashboard overview where real-time monitoring will take precedence. In this case, the system collects data from the database in order to display real-time intelligence feed, bullying incidents reports, and alerts. This enables continuous monitoring of the learning environment. At the end of the process, the user logs out of the system.

text: The student process offers a full range of tools that enable one to communicate their feelings and report any incidents. After going through the process of safe sign-in, there are two main options available. With the Safe Space model, one can post messages regarding their emotions. This tool enables one to decide whether they wish to contact a guardian or keep the record anonymous. The use of an organized gateway makes it possible for the person to identify themselves as victims or spectators in the incident. Depending on this, certain information will be entered such as the names of the victims or bullies involved. Attachments will then be uploaded to the database.

text: The proposed deployment will see students and counselors use a CodeIgniter 4 PHP-applications running on InfinityFree. This Hosting Company takes care of the Web server and the MySQL Database. Passwords will be hash-coded, audit records will be kept, plus vent submissions will be encrypted. It is set to be encrypted using AES-256 encryption from the set up prior to adding any raw text or bullying report. This will ensure that those without authorization to access the database will only be able to see random lengths of strings. This process will be done when updating a web application: push updates directly to web application via FTP, and clear system caches. The Hosting is free and for this reason, during the project phase is an opportunity for the project to be hosted at low cost provided that during the Test phase the code does not impose any restrictions on the type of Hosting used. If the school decides to expand the budget, or more users are needed for the system, the user can host the application and database for a fee at a different host (HostGator, AWS, DigitalOcean, etc.) and connect it to the custom domain name; the program need not be altered.

text: The machine power will play a significant role in the machine learning features allowing to run models (in the case of the machine learning features this will be Mdeberta, Go Emotions and the FAISS vector memory). As a result, the machine learning service employs a distinct entry and exit points as compared to the web app. The ML Engine is a containerized Python service built with FastAPI, running inside a Docker Container hosted on Hugging Face Spaces. The environment is stable and updates are easier thanks to running the service within a Docker container. Using Python scripts, the deployment is automated, whereby the older versions of the containers are removed to save disk space, other containers are zipped and transferred via SFTP, and the models are pushed into a Docker container via Hugging Face. However, on restarts, regardless of whether they are intentional or not, the API will continue to function. Last but not least, the system is interfaced with the device for the emergency notification purposes. For these regular email alerts which it transmits to parents and counselors via the Gmail SMTP protocol with an app password. If it is an emergency, the webapplication will send messages to the mobile phone, that will also be running an application for SMS-gateway within the local network. This phone will read the numbers out loud, and will text the parents/counsellors right away.

text: The implementation plan is a timeline of 10 months for the construction, deployment and testing of StudentShield. There are five phases of the project: Planning, System Coding, Debugging, System testing and user Acceptance Testing. During the three phases, each of the three key areas (Web app, ML service, automated alerts) are given a focus to ensure they operate in a coordinated system before the system goes live.

Analysis of quantitative data gathered through evaluation of users will be accomplished through descriptive statistics. text: For an efficient evaluation of the StudentShield prototype, the following data collection techniques will be used by the researchers in assessing the design and usability of the prototype. The first approach that will be applied is the Questionnaire/Survey. This will require the utilization of ISO 25010 quality criteria when assessing the functionality, reliability, usability, and efficiency of the prototype. The second approach that will be applied is the Interview. The qualitative information will be gathered through this approach concerning the alerting functionalities of the prototype for the school staff members. The third approach that will be employed is the Observation. The usability of the mockup of the dashboard and the report form will be evaluated using this method by means of guided testing. Finally, the Document review approach will be adopted in order to determine whether the data fields and workflow of the prototype match those of the school guidance counseling manuals and paper forms.

text: The site or location wherein the research was conducted consists of the Saint Vincent Blessed School of Manila (SVBSM). This is the official Name of the organization that was partnered for the conduct of the experiment. Its Address / location is 732 Instruccion St., Sampaloc, Manila, 1000 Metro Manila. The Type of organization is a private learning institution that caters to the needs of junior high school students. The Number of employees/users in the organization includes those in the guidance counseling office and IT department that ensure the welfare of the junior high school students. The description of the environment where the system was applied or tested includes the selection of SVBSM as the main site of research because it was the client. The school administration collaborated with the researchers to come up with an incident reporting system that caters to their real-life problems.
